registration_authorization: User requested generation and direct registration of all 80 questions.

questions.question_text: Complete the definite phrase “____ πόρτα” (the door) in the nominative singular.
questions.explanation: Feminine singular nominative definite article is η. Compare η γάτα (the cat).

questions.question_text: Complete “____ βιβλίο” (the book) with the nominative singular definite article.
questions.explanation: Neuter singular nominative definite article is το. Compare το σπίτι (the house).

questions.question_text: Complete “____ σκύλος” (the dog) with the nominative singular definite article.
questions.explanation: Masculine singular nominative definite article is ο. Compare ο φίλος (the friend).

questions.question_text: Complete “Εγώ ____ εδώ” (I am here).
questions.explanation: First-person singular of είμαι (be) is είμαι. Compare Είμαι καλά (I am well).

questions.question_text:
Translate into English.

```text
Το σπίτι
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Σπίτι (spíti) is house. Το marks the phrase as definite.

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
Η γάτα πίνει.
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Γάτα (gáta) is cat and πίνει (píni) means drinks.

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
Ο Νίκος γράφει.
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Γράφει (gráfi) means writes. The Greek article before a name usually disappears in English.

questions.question_text:
Choose the missing letter in the Greek word for water.

```text
νερ____
```
questions.explanation: The word is νερό (neró), with the stress on its final vowel.

questions.question_text: A card shows “γάτα” (cat). Count the written letters using $2+2$. How many are there?
questions.explanation: Γ-ά-τ-α are four letters. The accent is part of the vowel letter, so it adds no letter.

questions.question_text: A card shows “νερό” (water). Count the two syllables as $1+1$. Which split preserves both?
questions.explanation: Νερό (neró) syllabifies as νε-ρό. Each written syllable here contains a vowel.

questions.question_text: The phrase “το βιβλίο” contains $2+6$ letters if the space is ignored. Which total is correct?
questions.explanation: Το has two letters and βιβλίο (vivlío) has six. Stress marks do not add letters.

questions.question_text: A letter card shows uppercase Λ and lowercase λ. With $2-1=1$ distinct alphabet letter after matching case, which letter is it?
questions.explanation: Λ and λ are the two cases of lambda.

questions.question_text: Which is the lowercase partner of “Π”?
questions.explanation: Π and π are the uppercase and lowercase forms of pi.

questions.question_text: Which Greek letter represents the /m/ sound in “μαμά”?
questions.explanation: Μu, written μ, supplies /m/ in μαμά (mamá).

questions.question_text: Which Greek letter looks like Latin P in uppercase but represents /r/?
questions.explanation: Greek rho, Ρ or ρ, represents a Greek r sound.

questions.question_text: Which written vowel bears the stress in “τόπι”?
questions.explanation: The acute accent on ό marks the stress in τόπι (tópi), ball.

questions.question_text: Which letter is used for the final /s/ of “φίλος”?
questions.explanation: Lowercase sigma has the shape ς at the end of a word.

questions.question_text: What does “και” mean in “ο Νίκος και η Μαρία”?
questions.explanation: Και (ke) connects the two names and means and.

questions.question_text: Which Greek vowel letter is called omega?
questions.explanation: Omega is Ω or ω. Omicron is Ο or ο.

questions.question_text: Which Greek letter matches the /t/ sound in “τότε”?
questions.explanation: Tau, Τ or τ, has the /t/ sound in τότε (tóte), then.

questions.question_text: Complete the yes/no question “Εσύ ____ εδώ;” (Are you here?).
questions.explanation: Second-person singular of είμαι is είσαι. Compare Είσαι εκεί; (Are you there?).

questions.question_text: Complete “Η Μαρία ____ νερό” (Maria drinks water).
questions.explanation: Third-person singular present of πίνω is πίνει. Compare Ο Νίκος πίνει νερό.

questions.question_text: Make “Ο φίλος είναι εδώ” negative: “Ο φίλος ____ είναι εδώ.”
questions.explanation: Present indicative negation uses δεν before the finite verb. Compare Η γάτα δεν πίνει.

questions.question_text: Complete “Ο Νίκος διαβάζει ____ βιβλίο” to say he reads a book.
questions.explanation: Neuter singular indefinite article is ένα in both nominative and accusative. Compare Έχω ένα μολύβι (I have a pencil).

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
She reads the book.
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Διαβάζει (diavázi) is third-person reads. Βιβλίο (vivlío) means book.

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
Δεν είμαι εκεί.
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Εκεί (ekí) means there. Δεν είμαι marks the first-person negative.

questions.question_text:
Complete with the article before the name.

```text
____ Μαρία πίνει νερό
```
questions.explanation: The female name is the nominative subject, so Η is appropriate: Η Μαρία (i María).

questions.question_text:
Choose the stressed spelling for the Greek word meaning.

```text
milk
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Γάλα (gála) means milk and carries stress on its first vowel.

questions.question_text: In “ούτε” (neither), ου has $2$ letters representing $1$ vowel sound. Which sound does $2\to1$ indicate here?
questions.explanation: In ού-τε (úte), ου is the digraph for /u/. The accent appears on the second letter.

questions.question_text: In “βιβλίο”, separate the $6$ letters into $3$ consonant letters and the rest. How many vowel letters does $6-3$ give?
questions.explanation: The written form β-ι-β-λ-ί-ο has vowels at positions 2, 5 and 6.

questions.question_text: In “το νερό”, there are $2+4$ written letters. Removing the article leaves $6-2$ letters. Which is the remaining form?
questions.explanation: The noun νερό (neró) has four letters. Το is a separate two-letter article.

questions.question_text: The two words “σώμα” and “φως” contain $1+1$ lowercase sigmas. Which ordered shapes are used?
questions.explanation: In σώμα (sóma), sigma is first, so it is σ. In φως (fos), sigma is final, so it is ς.

questions.question_text: Which pronunciation matches “μπάλα” (ball) at the start of the word?
questions.explanation: Word-initial μπ represents /b/ in μπάλα (bála).

questions.question_text: What sound does “αι” represent in “και”?
questions.explanation: The digraph αι represents /e/ in και (ke).

questions.question_text: Which uppercase letter is the partner of lowercase “ξ”?
questions.explanation: Ξ/ξ is xi, which typically represents /ks/.

questions.question_text: What does the Greek semicolon-shaped mark in “Είναι εδώ;” signal?
questions.explanation: The Greek semicolon-shaped mark serves as the question mark in Είναι εδώ; (Is someone here?).

questions.question_text: A learner reads “Η Μαρία είναι εδώ” as if it started with an English h sound. How should the article sound?
questions.explanation: Modern Greek η is /i/. In η Μαρία (i María), it is the feminine definite article.

questions.question_text: Which word supplies the location in “Ο φίλος είναι εκεί”?
questions.explanation: Εκεί (ekí) means there. The other words make up the subject and verb.

questions.question_text: What does “Εγώ γράφω, εσύ διαβάζεις” say about the two people?
questions.explanation: Γράφω is I write, and διαβάζεις is you read when talking to one person.

questions.question_text: Which sound is shared by the first and last letters of “νέον”?
questions.explanation: Both positions use ν, which is nu and represents /n/. The word νέον is read néon.

questions.question_text: Complete “____ μαθητή βλέπει η Μαρία” to say Maria sees the male student.
questions.explanation: Masculine singular accusative definite article is τον. It marks the object even when fronted. Compare Τον φίλο βλέπει ο Νίκος.

questions.question_text: Complete “Η πόρτα είναι ____” using the correct form of red.
questions.explanation: Predicate adjective agreement: πόρτα is feminine singular, so use κόκκινη. Compare Η τσάντα είναι κόκκινη.

questions.question_text: Complete the phrase “____ γάτες” (the cats) as the subject of a sentence.
questions.explanation: Feminine nominative plural definite article is οι. Compare Οι πόρτες είναι εδώ.

questions.question_text: In “Ο Νίκος και η Μαρία ____ εδώ”, choose the verb meaning are.
questions.explanation: A coordinated third-person subject takes third-person plural είναι, which has the same form as third-person singular. Compare Η Άννα και ο Πέτρος είναι εδώ.

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
The dog has the ball.
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Έχει (échi) means has. Την μπάλα (tin bála) names the object.

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
Πού είναι το κλειδί;
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Πού (pú) asks where. Κλειδί (klidí) is key.

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
The pupil is not writing. He is reading.
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Ο μαθητής (o mathitís) is masculine. The negative applies to writes, followed by the positive verb reads.

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
Η Άννα βλέπει τον Νίκο.
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Η Άννα is the subject. Τον Νίκο is the masculine accusative object.

questions.question_text: The word “καιρός” (weather) includes $2$ letters in αι but they correspond to $1$ vowel sound. Which split keeps that pair together and separates the two syllables?
questions.explanation: Καιρός (kerós) has αι in its first syllable and stressed ό in its second.

questions.question_text: The word “ήλιος” has $5$ letters and begins with stressed η. Which reading places the stressed syllable at position $2-1$?
questions.explanation: The first accented letter is ή. In ήλιος (ílios), that is where the stressed syllable starts.

questions.question_text: “κόσμος” contains $2$ sigmas. If the first, at position $6-3$, is inside the word, which uppercase rendering makes both the same shape?
questions.explanation: Both σ and ς become capital Σ. Κόσμος means world or people, depending on context.

questions.question_text: In “σχολείο”, the written vowels are ο, ε, ί, ο. In careful pronunciation εί represents one vowel sound. Which ordered sequence of vowel sounds accounts for $4-1=3$?
questions.explanation: Σχολείο (scholío) has an /o/ on each side of the /i/ written εί.

questions.question_text: What contrast separates “πότε” from “ποτέ”?

options.A: Πότε means never. Ποτέ asks when.
options.C: Only ποτε without accent is a word.
options.D: Πότε asks when. Ποτέ means ever or, with negation, never.

questions.explanation: The stress differs: πότε (póte) is initial, while ποτέ (poté) is final.

questions.question_text: Which pair normally shares a vowel sound in Modern Greek?
questions.explanation: Both η and ι can represent /i/. Greek spelling preserves different letters for this sound.

questions.question_text: In “φαΐ” (food), what does the diaeresis over ι tell you?

options.A: The αι must be pronounced as a single /e/.
options.B: The α and ι are pronounced separately.

questions.explanation: In φαΐ (faí), the diaeresis prevents αι from being read as a single digraph.

questions.question_text: What is the initial sound of “ντομάτα” in standard Modern Greek?
questions.explanation: Word-initial ντ represents /d/ in ντομάτα (domáta).

questions.question_text: Which article tells you the grammatical role of “φίλο” in “Βλέπω τον φίλο”?

options.A: τον marks a feminine singular subject.
options.B: τον is a neuter plural article.
options.D: τον marks a masculine singular direct object.

questions.explanation: Τον φίλο is accusative and answers whom the speaker sees.

questions.question_text: What disappears in a natural English rendering of “Ο Πέτρος είναι εδώ”?

options.A: The definite article before the name.

questions.explanation: Greek commonly uses ο with a male personal name. English normally says Petros is here without the.

questions.question_text: A learner reads Greek “Β” as English b in “βιβλίο”. Which correction is accurate?

options.C: Modern Greek β is always silent.
options.D: Modern Greek β is identical in sound to μπ at the start of μπάλα.

questions.explanation: Β/β represents /v/ in βιβλίο (vivlío).

questions.question_text: What sound does “θ” begin with in “θέλω”?
questions.explanation: Theta represents /θ/ in θέλω (thélo), I want.

questions.question_text: Choose the phrase meaning “the small house” as the subject, with article and adjective both agreeing.
questions.explanation: Neuter singular noun-phrase agreement: το and μικρό agree with σπίτι. Compare το μικρό βιβλίο.

questions.question_text: Complete “Η Άννα βλέπει ____” to mean “Anna sees the woman”.
questions.explanation: Feminine singular accusative marks the object. Τη γυναίκα is standard without final ν before γ. Compare Τη γάτα βλέπει.

questions.question_text: Complete “Το σπίτι είναι ____ χωριό” to say the house is in the village.
questions.explanation: Contraction of σε with the neuter definite article το yields στο. Compare Το βιβλίο είναι στο σχολείο.

questions.question_text: Choose the standard neutral order for “Who is reading the book?” without placing special emphasis on “the book”.
questions.explanation: Interrogative subject ποιος asks who is doing the action. Compare Ποιος πίνει νερό; (Who drinks water?).

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
Το παιδί διαβάζει, αλλά δεν γράφει.
Answer: ____
```

options.A: The child writes, but does not read.
options.B: The child neither reads nor writes.
options.C: The child reads, but does not write.

questions.explanation: Διαβάζει (diavázi) is reads. Αλλά introduces contrast and δεν negates γράφει.

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
I see Maria, not Nikos.
Answer: ____
```

options.A: Με βλέπει η Μαρία, όχι ο Νίκος.
options.C: Βλέπω τον Νίκο, όχι τη Μαρία.
options.D: Βλέπω τη Μαρία, όχι τον Νίκο.

questions.explanation: Βλέπω means I see. Τη Μαρία and τον Νίκο are object forms, and όχι corrects which object is intended.

questions.question_text:
Translate.

```text
Where is the cat? It is not here.
Answer: ____
```

options.A: Πού είναι η γάτα; Δεν είναι εδώ.
options.B: Εδώ είναι η γάτα; Δεν είναι εκεί.
options.C: Πού είναι ο σκύλος; Δεν είναι εδώ.
options.D: Πού είναι η γάτα; Είναι εδώ.

questions.explanation: Πού asks where, and δεν είναι εδώ rejects the location here.

questions.question_text:
Choose the standard spelling of with stress on the penultimate syllable.

```text
lemon
Answer: ____
```
questions.explanation: Λεμόνι (lemóni) is the spelling. Its stressed ο is in the second-to-last syllable.

questions.question_text: A card counts vowel letters minus vowel sounds. In “και”, αι contributes $2-1=1$. Which stressed pair in “είμαι” contributes the same difference at the beginning of the word?
questions.explanation: In είμαι (íme), initial εί represents one /i/ sound and the accent marks that pair. The final unstressed αι separately represents one /e/ sound.

questions.question_text: Compare “παϊδάκι” with a spelling that removed the diaeresis. The original keeps $1+1$ vowel sounds across αϊ, rather than treating αι as one. Which reading preserves the original?

options.C: Skip α and read only ϊ.

questions.explanation: The diaeresis on ϊ preserves two vowel sounds in πα-ϊ-δά-κι (païdáki).

questions.question_text: A handwriting check gives one point for the correct initial of “φως” and one for the correct final sigma. Which spelling earns $1+1$ points?
questions.explanation: Φως (fos) starts with φ for /f/ and ends with lowercase final ς.

questions.question_text: For “αύριο” and “αυτό”, a reading rubric gives $1$ point per correctly decoded αυ pair. Which sequence earns $1+1$ points, in that order?
questions.explanation: In αύριο (ávrio), αυ precedes voiced ρ and sounds /av/. In αυτό (aftó), it precedes voiceless τ and sounds /af/.

questions.question_text: In “Πού πας;”, why is the accent on “Πού” useful?

options.A: It marks the interrogative word meaning where.
options.B: It makes που a plural article.
options.C: It indicates that the sentence is a command.
options.D: It changes the verb to the past.

questions.explanation: Interrogative πού (pú) is accented. Unaccented που has other uses, such as introducing a relative clause.

questions.question_text: Which analysis correctly separates script and grammar in “η Μαρία” and “οι φίλοι”?

options.B: The articles can sound alike, but η is feminine singular and οι is plural here.
options.C: Both articles use the same letters, but their sounds differ.
options.D: Η is plural and οι is a feminine singular object article.

questions.explanation: Η and οι both sound like /i/. The article spelling signals different grammatical forms.

questions.question_text: A note says “Ο Νίκος βλέπει τη Μαρία και η Μαρία βλέπει τον Νίκο.” What changes after και?

options.B: The verb changes to past tense.
options.C: The subject and object swap roles.
options.D: The second clause only describes Nikos's location.

questions.explanation: Ο Νίκος and η Μαρία are subject forms in different clauses. The accusative forms identify the objects.

questions.question_text: A learner says that the accent in “γάτα” is an extra letter. Which analysis is accurate?

options.A: It represents a consonant after γ.
options.B: It changes α into two separate vowels.
options.C: It indicates that the noun is plural.
options.D: It marks stress on the first vowel and adds no letter.

questions.explanation: Γάτα (gáta) has four letters. The accent on ά gives the stressed vowel.

questions.question_text: A learner types “σπίτισ” for a word whose intended final sound is /s/. Which edit fixes only sigma placement?

options.A: Change the last σ to ς.
options.B: Change the first σ to ς.
options.D: Replace the last σ with ζ.

questions.explanation: In lowercase, sigma uses σ before other letters and ς at the end of a word.

questions.question_text: Which comparison correctly illustrates how two spellings can share a Modern Greek vowel sound?
questions.explanation: Omicron and omega both represent /o/ in Modern Greek. The spelling still differs.

questions.question_text: What is the effect of changing “Ο μαθητής γράφει” to “Ο μαθητής γράφει;” in dialogue?

options.A: It changes the student from singular to plural.
options.C: It changes a statement into a yes/no question.

questions.explanation: The Greek question mark and spoken intonation can signal the question without changing the word order.

questions.question_text: Which response answers both parts of “Ποιος γράφει και πού;” if Nikos is writing at home?
questions.explanation: Ποιος asks for the person, and πού asks for the place. Ο Νίκος and στο σπίτι provide both.
